name: Anton Roman
life: “I still remember the first private detail I repeated too loudly at the desk.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Anton by a small Tuesday habit. Anton checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I had to tell a waiting patient why the counter was busy. I did it without turning another woman's history into entertainment.
appearance: Anton has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw. Look for close-cropped dark curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. In conversation Anton looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Anton has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Anton can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To keep the waiting line informed without disclosing the patient's history.
family: Marin Brady is Anton’s older relative by marriage. Anton asks before bringing somebody along. Marin can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The gift nobody wants*, Marin says, “I trained the daughter in tailoring. She told me exactly how little space her first shop needs.”
connections: Howard Starr. Two people at the hospital work out what other waiting patients actually need to be told.

reactions.situation: A family member asks to see both old folders
reactions.response: Anton checks what the patient has authorized before handing over either folder.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Anton asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.

reactions.response: Anton agrees on an amount both can bear losing before any cash changes hands.
reactions.asWritten: If a friend borrows money, Anton agrees on an amount both can bear losing before any cash changes hands.
